content.summary: Read a short report about rising prices and the choices facing a central bank and a government. You will practise identifying the main argument, finding evidence, and noticing how writers describe economic predictions and cause-and-effect relationships.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Use be likely to for cautious predictions, the present perfect passive to focus on policy actions, and if-clauses to explain possible economic results.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Learn terms for inflation, central bank decisions, government budgets, financial support and demand across an economy.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim the passage to find its main point. Then scan for figures, policy actions and cause-and-effect links. Check whether a prediction is certain or only possible.

learningObjectives: Identify the main idea in a report about inflation and economic policy.
Locate details about interest rates, government spending and household costs.
Understand how monetary and fiscal decisions may affect demand and prices.
Recognize cautious predictions, passive forms and conditional sentences in an economics text.

contextWarmup.prompt: If the cost of food and transport rises quickly, what might a central bank do to reduce pressure on prices?
options: Raise its benchmark interest rate
Set the price of every product in shops
Decide how much tax each household pays
contextWarmup.explanation: A central bank can raise its benchmark interest rate to make borrowing more expensive. This may reduce spending and slow price rises, although the effect is not immediate.

rules: Use be likely to + base verb to make a prediction that seems probable but is not certain: Borrowing is likely to become more expensive.
Use has or have been + past participle when the policy or action is more important than the person who carried it out: The rate has been increased.
Use if + present simple with will, may or could to explain a possible result: If borrowing costs rise, demand may fall. May and could show less certainty than will.

commonTrap.explanation: An economic report often describes a possible effect, not a guaranteed result. Do not treat words such as may, could or likely as statements of certainty.
commonTrap.wrong: If the central bank raises rates, inflation will certainly fall at once.
commonTrap.correct: If the central bank raises rates, inflation may fall over time.

content.contractionsSubtitle: Observe how subjects and verbs smoothly merge in everyday English:

contractions.subject: It
contractions.exampleFull: It is likely to take several months for higher rates to affect prices.
contractions.exampleContracted: It's likely to take several months for higher rates to affect prices.

contractions.subject: They
contractions.exampleFull: They have raised the benchmark rate twice this year.
contractions.exampleContracted: They've raised the benchmark rate twice this year.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Economic Predictions and Conditions
grammarFormulas.description: Use these sentence blocks to practise cautious predictions, policy reports and cause-and-effect statements:

subjects.label: The measure
subjects.role: Singular subject for a present perfect passive

complements.text: likely to rise if price pressures continue

items.exampleSentence: The annual inflation rate has risen above the central bank's target.
items.collocation: annual inflation rate / inflation rate target

items.exampleSentence: The central bank changed its monetary policy to control rising prices.
items.collocation: tighten monetary policy / monetary policy decision

items.exampleSentence: The fiscal deficit grew when public spending exceeded government income.
items.collocation: widening fiscal deficit / reduce a fiscal deficit

items.exampleSentence: The central bank used quantitative easing to support lending during the crisis.
items.collocation: use quantitative easing / quantitative easing programme

items.exampleSentence: Higher borrowing costs can reduce aggregate demand across the economy.
items.collocation: increase aggregate demand / fall in aggregate demand

items.collocation: raise the benchmark interest rate / hold the rate steady

items.exampleSentence: When prices rise faster than wages, households lose purchasing power.
items.collocation: protect purchasing power / household purchasing power

items.collocation: higher borrowing costs / borrowing costs rise

items.exampleSentence: Supply problems added to price pressure in the energy market.

content.passageTitle: The Cost of Bringing Inflation Down
paragraphs: In many countries, the cost of food, housing and transport has risen faster than wages. This means that households can buy less with the same income, even when they are still employed. A high inflation rate can have several causes, including expensive energy, supply problems and strong aggregate demand. Because these pressures do not all respond to the same solution, policymakers must consider their causes before acting.

Central banks often raise the benchmark interest rate as part of tighter monetary policy. If borrowing costs rise, families and businesses may spend less, and demand could cool over time. However, higher rates can also make mortgages and business loans more expensive. Governments can support households through public spending, but a large fiscal deficit may increase concerns about public debt. Measures have been introduced in some countries to ease immediate hardship, while central banks have tried to bring inflation down. Further rate rises are likely if price pressure persists, but the effects of any decision can take months to appear.

drills.prompt: Match each term to its meaning in the passage.

pairs.definition: The speed at which general prices rise
Central bank actions that influence money and interest rates
A situation in which government spending is greater than income
Total demand for goods and services in an economy
A central bank rate that guides other interest rates

drills.prompt: Complete the sentence: If borrowing costs rise, families and businesses ___ spend less.
options: may
has
was

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How policymakers respond to inflation and the possible effects of their choices
Why every country should use the same tax system
How households can avoid paying interest on loans
questions.answer: How policymakers respond to inflation and the possible effects of their choices
questions.explanation: The passage describes central bank interest-rate decisions, government spending and the effects these actions may have.

questions.question: What can happen to household purchasing power when prices rise faster than wages?
options: Households can buy less with the same income.
Households automatically receive higher wages.
The cost of transport and housing falls.
questions.answer: Households can buy less with the same income.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says households can buy less with the same income when costs rise faster than wages.

questions.question: Which group of factors is given as a possible cause of high inflation?
options: Expensive energy, supply problems and strong aggregate demand
Lower interest rates, smaller homes and less public debt
Higher wages, lower transport costs and reduced spending
questions.answer: Expensive energy, supply problems and strong aggregate demand
questions.explanation: The first paragraph lists expensive energy, supply problems and strong aggregate demand as possible causes.

questions.question: Why might a central bank raise its benchmark interest rate?
options: To make borrowing more expensive and potentially cool demand
To set the price of food and transport directly
To guarantee that wages rise at the same speed as prices
questions.answer: To make borrowing more expensive and potentially cool demand
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says higher borrowing costs may reduce spending and cool demand over time.

questions.question: What is one possible disadvantage of higher interest rates?
options: Mortgages and business loans can become more expensive.
Government income must immediately increase.
Supply problems are certain to disappear.
questions.answer: Mortgages and business loans can become more expensive.
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly notes that higher rates can make mortgages and business loans more expensive.

questions.question: What may a large fiscal deficit cause people to worry about?
options: Public debt
The supply of housing
Household employment contracts
questions.explanation: The passage says a large fiscal deficit may increase concerns about public debt.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Measures have been introduced in some countries,' what does the passive form emphasise?
options: The measures that were introduced
The people who introduced the measures
The date when the measures will end
questions.explanation: The passive construction places the focus on the measures. The passage does not name the people who introduced them.

questions.question: What does 'are likely to' suggest in 'Further rate rises are likely'?
options: The rises are probable, but not certain.
The rises have already happened.
The rises are impossible.
questions.answer: The rises are probable, but not certain.
questions.explanation: Likely expresses a cautious prediction rather than a guaranteed event.

questions.question: According to the passage, how soon can the effects of a policy decision appear?
options: They can take months to appear.
They always appear on the same day.
They appear only after several years.
questions.answer: They can take months to appear.
questions.explanation: The final sentence says that the effects of any decision can take months to appear.

questions.question: Why should policymakers consider the causes of inflation before acting?
options: Different pressures may not respond to the same solution.
All causes of inflation can be removed with one interest-rate change.
The government controls every price in the economy.
questions.answer: Different pressures may not respond to the same solution.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph explains that these pressures do not all respond to the same solution, so policymakers need to consider their causes.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Global Macroeconomics and Policy Dilemmas

content.summary: This briefing prepares you to track fast discussions on macroeconomic policy, central bank actions, and fiscal trade-offs. You will practice isolating high-level economic collocations and catching phonological reductions in natural dialogue between young professionals.
learningObjectives: Catch key economic indicators and policy proposals in rapid speech
Identify causal links between interest rate shifts and market reactions
Notice consonant elisions and linking sounds in professional conversations

keyPhrases.note: Used when central banks increase policy rates to cool down inflation.
Describes an unintended economic slowdown caused by sudden shocks or aggressive tightening.
The gap created when public spending exceeds government revenue.
The total demand for all finished goods and services produced in an economy.

connectedSpeech.note: Vowels in auxiliary 'have' and pronoun 'you' reduce to weak schwas in rapid questions.
The alveolar plosive /t/ is omitted between consonant sounds.
The final consonant /k/ carries directly over to the indefinite article schwa.
The /p/ remains unreleased before the following fricative /ʃ/.

sections.title: Audio Dialogue: Sidewalk Analysis at the Jakarta Summit

content.context: Alex, a ministry analyst, and Morgan, a central bank researcher, grab coffee outside an international economic forum in Jakarta.
content.audioPrompt: Listen to Alex and Morgan discuss rising inflation, interest rates, and fiscal trade-offs.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Have you seen the latest numbers?

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: Yes, they jumped past seven percent.
lines.translation: Ya, angkanya melonjak melampaui tujuh persen.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Central banks must raise benchmark rates.
lines.translation: Bank sentral harus menaikkan suku bunga acuan.

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: Aggressive hikes could spark a recession.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Consumer spending will drop sharply too.
lines.translation: Belanja konsumen juga akan turun tajam.

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: Governments are still expanding public budgets.
lines.translation: Pemerintah masih terus memperluas anggaran publik.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Higher subsidies widen the fiscal deficit.
lines.translation: Subsidi yang lebih tinggi memperlebar defisit fiskal.

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: That fuels even more price pressure.
lines.translation: Hal itu semakin memicu tekanan harga.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Targeted support is a safer approach.
lines.translation: Dukungan yang terarah adalah pendekatan yang lebih aman.

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: Gradual tightening protects overall economic growth.
lines.translation: Pengetatan bertahap melindungi pertumbuhan ekonomi secara keseluruhan.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: We must balance aggregate demand carefully.
lines.translation: Kita harus menyeimbangkan permintaan agregat dengan hati-hati.

lines.speaker: Morgan
lines.text: Exactly, or growth will stall completely.
lines.translation: Tepat sekali, jika tidak pertumbuhan akan terhenti total.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Macroeconomic Policy Analysis and Forecasting

content.summary: This guide outlines essential writing structures for macroeconomic policy reviews, economic forecasts, and cause-and-effect explanations. Professional economic writing requires objective tone, clear cause-and-effect linkages, and precise hedging.

blueprintItems.title: Hedged Economic Forecasting
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + is/are + likely to + base verb
blueprintItems.example: Interest rates are likely to rise if inflationary pressures persist throughout the fiscal year.

blueprintItems.title: Policy Implementation in Passive Voice
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + has/have been + past participle + by + agent
blueprintItems.example: Quantitative easing measures have been implemented by the central bank to stimulate economic growth.

blueprintItems.title: Conditional Economic Mechanisms
blueprintItems.formula: If + Subject + present simple, Subject + will/may/could + base verb
blueprintItems.example: If the government tightens fiscal policy, consumer spending could decline significantly in the short term.

mechanicsRules.rule: Place a comma after an introductory conditional clause that begins a sentence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: If inflation accelerates the central bank will raise borrowing costs immediately.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: If inflation accelerates, the central bank will raise borrowing costs immediately.
mechanicsRules.why: When the dependent 'if' clause precedes the independent clause, a comma is required to separate the condition from the consequence.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize formal names of public monetary institutions, but lowercase general references.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The Federal reserve announced new guidelines, whereas another Central Bank hesitated.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The Federal Reserve announced new guidelines, whereas another central bank hesitated.
mechanicsRules.why: Specific official titles such as 'Federal Reserve' or 'European Central Bank' are proper nouns, while generic references like 'central bank' are common nouns.

mechanicsRules.rule: Hyphenate compound adjectives that precede the noun they modify in economic contexts.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The bank adopted a short term strategy to tackle demand pull inflation.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The bank adopted a short-term strategy to tackle demand-pull inflation.
mechanicsRules.why: Compound modifiers placed before a noun require hyphens to clarify that the words function as a single descriptive unit.

sampleSentences.en: Central banks are likely to raise benchmark interest rates to combat rising inflation.
sampleSentences.id: Bank sentral kemungkinan akan menaikkan suku bunga acuan untuk memerangi kenaikan inflasi.

sampleSentences.en: Unprecedented fiscal stimulus measures have been approved by the ministry of finance.
sampleSentences.id: Tindakan stimulus fiskal yang belum pernah terjadi sebelumnya telah disetujui oleh kementerian keuangan.

sampleSentences.en: If borrowing costs increase sharply, commercial investment will probably slow down over the next two quarters.
sampleSentences.id: Jika biaya pinjaman meningkat tajam, investasi komersial kemungkinan akan melambat selama dua kuartal berikutnya.

sampleSentences.en: Supply chain bottlenecks are likely to ease once manufacturing hubs resume full capacity.
sampleSentences.id: Hambatan rantai pasokan kemungkinan akan mereda setelah pusat manufaktur beroperasi pada kapasitas penuh.
sampleSentences.focus: Hedged prediction with dependent time clause

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Analyze an Interest Rate Decision
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three to four sentences evaluating how a higher benchmark interest rate influences corporate investment and consumer behavior. Use a hedged forecast with 'is/are likely to' and at least one passive construction describing policy implementation.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Higher interest rates have been introduced by the monetary committee to cool down an overheating economy. Commercial borrowers are likely to face steeper loan repayments over the coming fiscal quarters. Consequently, major capital expenditure projects are likely to be postponed by corporate leaders until credit markets stabilize.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Begin typing your economic analysis here...

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Outline an Inflationary Scenario
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Draft a short paragraph forecasting the consequences of rising commodity prices on domestic inflation. Use an introductory conditional clause starting with 'If' and modal hedging such as 'could' or 'may'.
guidedLabChallenges.example: If international energy prices climb unexpectedly, transportation and manufacturing expenses will rise across the domestic economy. Retail businesses may pass these operational costs directly onto household consumers. Under these conditions, core inflation could stay above target levels for several consecutive quarters.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Begin typing your scenario forecast here...

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence in the passive voice using the specified structure: 'Subject + has/have been + past participle + by + agent'.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The central bank has adjusted the reserve requirement ratio.
targetAnswers: The reserve requirement ratio has been adjusted by the central bank.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In the present perfect passive voice, singular subjects take 'has been' followed by the past participle 'adjusted' and the agent phrase 'by the central bank'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the definitive forecast into a hedged economic prediction using 'is likely to' or 'are likely to'.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Inflation will decrease steadily throughout the third quarter.
practicumQuestions.hint: Replace 'will decrease' with 'is likely to decrease'.
targetAnswers: Inflation is likely to decrease steadily throughout the third quarter.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Because macroeconomic projections carry uncertainty, financial analysts replace definitive modal verbs like 'will' with hedged constructions like 'is likely to'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences into a single first conditional statement starting with 'If'.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The government reduces income tax. Consumer spending will expand rapidly.
practicumQuestions.hint: Begin with 'If the government reduces', and remember to place a comma between clauses.
targetAnswers: If the government reduces income tax, consumer spending will expand rapidly.
practicumQuestions.explanation: When an introductory conditional clause opens the sentence, a comma must separate it from the main clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the punctuation and capitalization errors in the following sentence.
practicumQuestions.promptText: if the bank of england raises rates commercial lenders will follow immediately.
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first word and proper institution name, and insert a comma after the conditional clause.
targetAnswers: If the Bank of England raises rates, commercial lenders will follow immediately.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Proper institution names like 'Bank of England' require capitalization, the sentence must start with a capital letter, and a comma is required after the 'if' clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence in the passive voice with an explicit agent phrase.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Parliament has approved a comprehensive fiscal recovery plan.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'A comprehensive fiscal recovery plan'.
targetAnswers: A comprehensive fiscal recovery plan has been approved by Parliament.
A comprehensive fiscal recovery plan has been approved by parliament.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Move the direct object to the subject position, use 'has been approved', and add 'by Parliament' at the end.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Convert the absolute statement into a hedged prediction using 'are likely to'.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Commercial banks will raise mortgage rates in response to tightening liquidity.
practicumQuestions.hint: Substitute 'will raise' with 'are likely to raise'.
targetAnswers: Commercial banks are likely to raise mortgage rates in response to tightening liquidity.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Plural subjects take 'are likely to' followed by the base verb form 'raise' to convey analytical caution.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the sentences into one statement using 'if' in the middle of the sentence without a comma.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Economic growth may contract during the next quarter. Export demand drops sharply.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'Economic growth may contract' followed directly by 'if'.
targetAnswers: Economic growth may contract during the next quarter if export demand drops sharply.
practicumQuestions.explanation: When the conditional clause follows the main clause, no comma is required before 'if'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the subject-verb agreement and punctuation in the following sentence.
practicumQuestions.promptText: supply chain disruptions is likely to keep manufacturing costs elevated
practicumQuestions.hint: Ensure the verb agrees with the plural subject 'disruptions' and finish with a period.
targetAnswers: Supply chain disruptions are likely to keep manufacturing costs elevated.
Supply-chain disruptions are likely to keep manufacturing costs elevated.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The subject 'Supply chain disruptions' is plural, so it requires 'are likely to' rather than 'is likely to', along with initial capitalization and a final period.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the active voice sentence into the passive voice with an agent phrase.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The monetary authorities have introduced stricter reserve mandates.
targetAnswers: Stricter reserve mandates have been introduced by the monetary authorities.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Because 'Stricter reserve mandates' is plural, use 'have been introduced' followed by 'by the monetary authorities'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the economic prediction by writing a full independent clause starting with 'consumer borrowing is likely to...':
practicumQuestions.promptText: If interest rates continue to climb this year, [complete with a hedged prediction about consumer borrowing].
practicumQuestions.hint: Write a complete sentence including the 'if' clause and ending with 'consumer borrowing is likely to drop' or 'decline'.
targetAnswers: If interest rates continue to climb this year, consumer borrowing is likely to decline.
If interest rates continue to climb this year, consumer borrowing is likely to drop.
If interest rates continue to climb this year, consumer borrowing is likely to decrease.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The completed sentence pairs an introductory conditional clause with a grammatically correct hedged prediction ('consumer borrowing is likely to decline/drop/decrease').

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Inflation and Policy Choices

content.summary: Practise explaining how inflation, interest rates, and fiscal decisions affect households and businesses. Use precise economic collocations, support your opinions with reasons, and make clear distinctions between causes, effects, and policy responses.
content.audioGuidance: Say longer economic terms in syllable groups, then blend them at a natural pace. Give key information words clear stress. Use falling intonation to finish statements and rising intonation for genuine yes-or-no questions. Pause briefly before giving a contrast or consequence.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Keep vowel sounds distinct in terms such as rate, debt, and demand.
pillars.explanation: Avoid shortening important vowels so much that technical words become difficult to recognise. Practise each word slowly, then use it in a full sentence.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.target: Place the main stress correctly in multi-syllable economic vocabulary.
pillars.explanation: Words such as inflation and monetary have a clear stressed syllable. Mark the stressed part while practising, then keep that stress when speaking at normal speed.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.target: Emphasise the policy, change, or result you want listeners to notice.
pillars.explanation: In a sentence such as “The central bank raised the benchmark interest rate,” give the main information words more prominence than articles and auxiliary verbs.

pillars.name: Intonation and Pausing
pillars.target: Use a clear falling tone for conclusions and a rising tone for questions.
pillars.explanation: A brief pause before phrases such as “as a result” or “on the other hand” helps listeners follow your reasoning.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Keep the main word stress on the second syllable of inflation. In the phrase, rate also receives stress because it carries important information.
Monetary is stressed on its first syllable. Policy also has first-syllable stress.
Aggregate has first-syllable stress, while demand is stressed on its second syllable.
Quantitative is stressed on its first syllable, while easing is stressed on its first syllable.

drills.targetText: The inflation rate has risen above the central bank's target.
drills.phonetic: /ði ɪnˈfleɪʃən reɪt hæz ˈrɪzən əˈbʌv ðə ˈsentrəl bæŋks ˈtɑːɡɪt/
drills.focus: Stress in inflation rate and clear final consonants.
drills.hint: Give inflation stress on its second syllable, and finish target with a clear /t/.

drills.targetText: A higher benchmark interest rate may reduce aggregate demand.
drills.phonetic: /ə ˈhaɪə ˈbentʃmɑːk ˈɪntrəst reɪt meɪ rɪˈdjuːs ˈæɡrɪɡət dɪˈmɑːnd/
drills.focus: Sentence stress and the contrast between aggregate and demand.
drills.hint: Emphasise higher, interest rate, reduce, and demand, while keeping short grammar words light.

drills.targetText: The government could address the fiscal deficit by changing public spending.
drills.phonetic: /ðə ˈɡʌvənmənt kʊd əˈdres ðə ˈfɪskəl ˈdefɪsɪt baɪ ˈtʃeɪndʒɪŋ ˈpʌblɪk ˈspendɪŋ/
drills.focus: Clear syllable stress in address, fiscal deficit, and spending.
drills.hint: Stress the second syllable of address and keep the final consonants in deficit and spending audible.

drills.targetText: Quantitative easing can increase liquidity, but it may also raise asset prices.
drills.phonetic: /ˌkwɒntɪˈteɪtɪv ˈiːzɪŋ kən ɪnˈkriːs lɪˈkwɪdəti bət ɪt meɪ ˈɔːlsəʊ reɪz ˈæset ˈpraɪsɪz/
drills.focus: Long-word stress and a clear contrast before but.
drills.hint: Say quantitative in syllable groups, pause briefly before but, and finish the statement with falling intonation.

roleplay.context: You are taking part in a live call between a central bank economist and a small-business representative. Discuss rising prices, the benchmark interest rate, and the likely effects of a policy change.

turns.speaker: Central Bank Economist
turns.text: The inflation rate remains above our target. How are higher prices affecting your business?
turns.translation: Tingkat inflasi masih berada di atas target kami. Bagaimana kenaikan harga memengaruhi bisnis Anda?

turns.speaker: Small-Business Representative
turns.text: Our costs have risen, and customers are spending less. A higher benchmark interest rate could make borrowing even more difficult.
turns.translation: Biaya kami meningkat, dan pelanggan berbelanja lebih sedikit. Suku bunga acuan yang lebih tinggi dapat membuat pinjaman semakin sulit.

turns.speaker: Central Bank Economist
turns.text: That is a concern. Do you think weaker aggregate demand would bring prices down, or would it put jobs at risk?
turns.translation: Itu menjadi kekhawatiran. Menurut Anda, apakah permintaan agregat yang lebih lemah akan menurunkan harga, atau justru membahayakan pekerjaan?

turns.speaker: Small-Business Representative
turns.text: It could slow price rises, but the government should also consider targeted support rather than increasing the fiscal deficit without a clear plan.
turns.translation: Hal itu dapat memperlambat kenaikan harga, tetapi pemerintah juga sebaiknya mempertimbangkan bantuan yang terarah daripada meningkatkan defisit fiskal tanpa rencana yang jelas.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds. Describe a recent or imagined period of rising prices and explain how it affected people.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell a short story about how an increase in the inflation rate affected a household or a local business.
storyPoints: Describe what prices increased and how people first noticed the change.
Explain how the change affected spending, saving, or business costs.
Say what action the household or business took and what happened next.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: When the inflation rate rose, the shop's costs increased, so the owner put off buying new equipment.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /wen ði ɪnˈfleɪʃən reɪt rəʊz, ðə ʃɒps kɒsts ɪnˈkriːst, səʊ ði ˈəʊnə pʊt ɒf ˈbaɪɪŋ njuː ɪˈkwɪpmənt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Organise the account in time order and use past forms to describe the situation, its effects, and the response.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds. Tell a cause-and-effect story about a central bank decision and its possible impact.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe a situation in which a central bank changes interest rates and explain how households or firms respond.
storyPoints: Explain what happened to inflation or economic growth before the decision.
Describe the change to the benchmark interest rate and the reason for it.
Explain one possible effect on borrowing, aggregate demand, or employment.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The central bank raised its benchmark interest rate to slow borrowing, although the decision may also reduce investment.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈsentrəl bæŋk reɪzd ɪts ˈbentʃmɑːk ˈɪntrəst reɪt tə sləʊ ˈbɒrəʊɪŋ, ɔːlˈðəʊ ðə dɪˈsɪʒən meɪ ˈɔːlsəʊ rɪˈdjuːs ɪnˈvestmənt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Make the sequence of events clear and use linking language to show both an intended result and a possible drawback.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. Respond to the other speaker, explain your view, and ask at least one relevant question.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: You are speaking with a central bank economist about whether to raise the benchmark interest rate.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A central bank economist is consulting a business representative before announcing a possible interest-rate rise. Discuss inflation pressures and the likely effects on borrowing and demand.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a small-business representative. Explain how borrowing costs affect your business and ask the economist how the decision could affect inflation.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: A higher benchmark interest rate could reduce inflation, but it may also make investment more expensive for small firms.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ə ˈhaɪə ˈbentʃmɑːk ˈɪntrəst reɪt kʊd rɪˈdjuːs ɪnˈfleɪʃən, bət ɪt meɪ ˈɔːlsəʊ meɪk ɪnˈvestmənt mɔːr ɪkˈspensɪv fə smɔːl fɜːmz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Answer the economist directly, give a reason or example, and ask a follow-up question to keep the exchange interactive.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. State a position, respond to a challenge, and support your view with a reason.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Discuss whether the government should increase public spending when the economy is slowing.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A finance journalist is interviewing a policy adviser about a slowing economy, public spending, and the fiscal deficit.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the policy adviser. Explain whether targeted spending could support aggregate demand, while recognising the risk of a larger fiscal deficit.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Targeted public spending may support aggregate demand, although it could widen the fiscal deficit.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈtɑːɡɪtɪd ˈpʌblɪk ˈspendɪŋ meɪ səˈpɔːt ˈæɡrɪɡət dɪˈmɑːnd, ɔːlˈðəʊ ɪt kʊd ˈwaɪdən ðə ˈfɪskəl ˈdefɪsɪt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Present a balanced view by describing a possible benefit as well as a budgetary risk.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live interview. Clarify a technical policy and explain its intended effect in accessible language.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: A radio host asks you to explain quantitative easing and why a central bank might use it.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A radio host is interviewing an economist after the central bank announces an asset-purchase programme.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the economist. Explain what quantitative easing involves and describe one way it may encourage borrowing or investment.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Quantitative easing involves central bank asset purchases intended to add liquidity and encourage lending.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˌkwɒntɪˈteɪtɪv ˈiːzɪŋ ɪnˈvɒlvz ˈsentrəl bæŋk ˈæset ˈpɜːtʃəsɪz ɪnˈtendɪd tə æd lɪˈkwɪdəti ænd ɪnˈkʌrɪdʒ ˈlendɪŋ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Define the policy in plain English, then connect the action to a likely effect on the financial system.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live call with an analyst. Compare possible outcomes and give a cautious prediction.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: An analyst asks whether lower interest rates would quickly increase aggregate demand.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are on a call with an economic analyst discussing a possible rate cut during a period of weak growth.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a market analyst. Explain how lower rates could affect borrowing and spending, while noting why the effect may take time.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Lower interest rates could encourage borrowing, but weak confidence may limit the rise in aggregate demand.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈləʊə ˈɪntrəst reɪts kʊd ɪnˈkʌrɪdʒ ˈbɒrəʊɪŋ, bət wiːk ˈkɒnfɪdəns meɪ ˈlɪmɪt ðə raɪz ɪn ˈæɡrɪɡət dɪˈmɑːnd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use cautious language such as could or may, and explain why a policy change might not produce an immediate result.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds. Use inflation rate, fiscal deficit, and aggregate demand accurately in connected sentences.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Explain how high inflation and a large fiscal deficit could affect aggregate demand.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: A high inflation rate can weaken purchasing power, while a large fiscal deficit may affect demand through government spending.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ə haɪ ɪnˈfleɪʃən reɪt kən ˈwiːkən ˈpɜːtʃəsɪŋ ˈpaʊə, waɪl ə lɑːdʒ ˈfɪskəl ˈdefɪsɪt meɪ əˈfekt dɪˈmɑːnd θruː ˈɡʌvənmənt ˈspendɪŋ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Show that you understand the terms by using each one in a relevant economic relationship, not as a list.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the prompt aloud with two conditional sentences. Use if or unless to describe possible policy effects.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: What might happen if the central bank raised the benchmark interest rate, and what might happen if it did not?
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If the central bank raised the benchmark interest rate, borrowing might fall; unless inflation eased, further action could be considered.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪf ðə ˈsentrəl bæŋk reɪzd ðə ˈbentʃmɑːk ˈɪntrəst reɪt, ˈbɒrəʊɪŋ maɪt fɔːl; ənˈles ɪnˈfleɪʃən iːzd, ˈfɜːðər ˈækʃən kʊd bi kənˈsɪdəd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a past simple form after if to describe a hypothetical situation, then use might or could for its possible result.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say each phrase three times, keeping the main word stress clear. Then use all three phrases in one short explanation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Practise monetary policy, inflation rate, and quantitative easing with clear syllable stress.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Monetary policy may change the inflation rate, while quantitative easing can add liquidity.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈmɒnɪtəri ˈpɒləsi meɪ tʃeɪndʒ ði ɪnˈfleɪʃən reɪt, waɪl ˌkwɒntɪˈteɪtɪv ˈiːzɪŋ kən æd lɪˈkwɪdəti/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Keep the main stress on the first syllable of monetary and policy, the second syllable of inflation, and the first syllable of easing.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the question with rising intonation, then say the conclusion with falling intonation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Practise asking whether a rate rise will reduce inflation, then give a clear concluding statement.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Will a higher interest rate reduce inflation? It may also slow borrowing and demand.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /wɪl ə ˈhaɪər ˈɪntrəst reɪt rɪˈdjuːs ɪnˈfleɪʃən? ɪt meɪ ˈɔːlsəʊ sləʊ ˈbɒrəʊɪŋ ænd dɪˈmɑːnd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Let your voice rise at the end of the yes-or-no question. Use a falling tone to finish the final statement.
